result.title: HarnessFlow: MCTS-Guided Harness Optimization for LLM Agents
result.summary: The performance of large language model (LLM) agents depends on both the underlying model and the harness that governs interaction with tools and the environment. Yet harness design remains largely manual, and automating it requires navigating an open-ended search space through costly end-to-end evaluations. We introduce HarnessFlow, a framework for optimizing complete executable harnesses under a limited candidate-evaluation budget, with the model and task environment held fixed. HarnessFlow organizes candidates and their evaluation histories in a refinement tree, using a Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS)-based policy to balance exploitation and exploration. A coding agent refines selected harnesses using archived code, execution feedback, and a library of reusable harness mechanisms. With 15 refinement attempts per benchmark, HarnessFlow achieves the highest mean test scores among the compared methods on six benchmarks spanning agentic tasks, coding, and web interaction. The optimized harnesses achieve an average score of 69.48%, outperforming the initial harnesses and Meta-Harness by 10.89 and 3.95 percentage points, respectively, while incurring lower average per-task execution costs than hand-engineered baselines. These results suggest that structured harness search offers a promising route toward automating the design of capable and efficient LLM agents.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 HarnessFlow，在固定模型与任务环境的前提下，用 MCTS 组织候选 harness 的改进树，并由编码智能体结合代码、执行反馈与可复用机制库迭代改写，在每基准 15 次尝试的预算内于六个基准上超过初始 harness 与 Meta-Harness。
AI.relevance_reason: harness 决定工具调用与环境交互流程，与 LVR 中「何时 LOOK、何时 STOP」的控制策略有概念对应；其预算受限的候选搜索与执行反馈改进，可供核查能否迁移到 latent 推理流程的自动配置与评价，但论文本身不涉及视觉输入或内部状态。
